title: Localized derived tensor model independence across derived-category universes
statement: Let R, A, B, D be commutative rings in one universe u, with R-algebras A and B and an (A tensor_R B)-algebra D. Let Q be an integer-indexed cochain complex of A-modules. Choose HasDerivedCategory structures for ModuleCat R and ModuleCat B in a morphism universe w, and another pair of such structures in a possibly different morphism universe wprime. For any base-derived tensor cohomology models m and n [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model] of Q with final coefficients D formed using the first and second pairs respectively, and every integer i, there is a D-linear isomorphism s from D tensor_(A tensor_R B) m.cohomology(i) to D tensor_(A tensor_R B) n.cohomology(i) satisfying s.hom followed by n.localizedComparison(i) equals m.localizedComparison(i). No flatness, localization, boundedness, or K-flatness of Q is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 15.61.1, independence of derived tensor choices; identity coefficient-equivalence case of the restricted ring comparison.

proof.text: Apply exists_baseDerivedTensor_restricted_ring_comparison with identity equivalences of R, A, B and A tensor_R B, and canonical identity restriction chain isomorphisms for Q and its ordinary tensor complex. This supplies the second-ring-linear isomorphism kB, its A-action equation, and the ordinary comparison equation.

Use B-linearity of kB and its A-action equation. Write each pure coefficient a tensor b as (a tensor 1)(1 tensor b), then use tensor induction to prove A tensor_R B-linearity. Its additive bijectivity gives a tensor-algebra-linear isomorphism e.

Prove that the exact homology isomorphism for the identity functor has identity hom component by comparing mapped and original left homology data with identity maps. NatTrans.app_homology for the identity restriction inverse then identifies homology of the canonical identity restriction chain map with the inverse exact restriction homology map on underlying elements. It is injective because it is the homology of a chain isomorphism. Apply that injectivity to the ordinary comparison equation to obtain e.hom followed by n.comparison equals m.comparison.

The models ordinaryToLocalized maps coincide by their specified pure-tensor formulas and ExtendScalars.hom_ext. Extend e to D. Transpose the desired square through extension/restriction adjunction, use naturality on the left and both localized_eq identities, and substitute the ordinary comparison equation and equality of ordinaryToLocalized maps. Associativity closes the square.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 15.61.1, specialized to identity ring transport and then scalar extension to D.

lean.statement:
theorem baseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel_localized_universe_independence
    (R A B D : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing D]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra (A ⊗[R] B) D]
    [dR : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    [dB : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} B)]
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (m : @BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel.{u, u, u, u, u, w}
      R A B _ _ _ _ _ dR dB Q D _ _)
    [dR' : HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    [dB' : HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{u} B)]
    (n : @BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel.{u, u, u, u, u, w'}
      R A B _ _ _ _ _ dR' dB' Q D _ _) (i : ℤ) :
    ∃ s : (extendScalars (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) D)).obj
        (@BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel.cohomology R A B _ _ _ _ _
          dR dB Q D _ _ m i) ≅
        (extendScalars (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) D)).obj
          (@BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel.cohomology R A B _ _ _ _ _
            dR' dB' Q D _ _ n i),
      s.hom ≫ (@BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel.localizedComparison R A B _ _ _ _ _
        dR' dB' Q D _ _ n i) =
          @BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel.localizedComparison R A B _ _ _ _ _
            dR dB Q D _ _ m i
